points.description: States one valid advantage of the observer that a filter cannot provide, with correct reasoning. Acceptable: it uses the known input u and plant model so it predicts rather than differentiates, tracking changing velocity without the lag/smoothing trade-off of a low-pass filter; OR it estimates an unmeasured state rather than just smoothing a differentiated measurement; OR quantisation enters through a bounded, filtered path rather than being divided by T. A bare claim (e.g. 'observer is better/more accurate') with no reasoning does not earn full marks.

levels.says: Names a valid advantage (e.g. uses the model/input u) but gives no or incorrect reasoning for why a filter cannot do it.

points.description: States one circumstance where the filter is safer, specifically invoking model error or parameter uncertainty: the filter is model-free, so when A, B or actuator gain are wrong/drifting (temperature, load, wear), or the plant is strongly nonlinear away from the linearisation point, the observer's estimate becomes biased or misleading/divergent while the filter only depends on its own bandwidth choice. A circumstance not tied to model error or uncertainty (e.g. 'filter is simpler', 'cheaper to compute') does not earn the mark.

levels.says: Says the filter is safer because it is model-free or simpler, but does not link this to an inaccurate or uncertain model/parameters as the circumstance.

rubric.notes: Full marks need one valid observer advantage with reasoning (1) and one filter-favouring circumstance tied to model error or parameter uncertainty (1). Part marks are given where the idea is named but the reasoning or the link to model error is missing. Generic statements such as 'observer is more accurate' or 'filter is easier' earn nothing.
